T01.reasoning: Square-with-cross on a base resembles the sheep sign family; it recurs in herd lists beside T36, T16, X0147, X1844, X1166.

T02.reasoning: Circle with side bars; appears inside multi-sign entries (X1310 T02 X1084 X1457), more like a name or title than a commodity.

T03.reasoning: Stepped rectangular outline may be a structure; it often closes entries (X1873 T03), plausibly a place or institution.

T04.reasoning: Chevron shapes may be fish tails; it occurs in lists with T17, T13, T38, X1394, X1350 that look like fish accounts.

T05.reasoning: Two grain ears next to a box look like barley plus a container or measure; it is counted with numbers in accounts.

T06.reasoning: Always comes last in the fixed herd sequence T36, X0147, X1844, T16, X1166, T06, so it is a small-cattle category.

T07.reasoning: A comb of strokes with a loop looks like a tied bundle; it is counted in alternation with X0829 entries.

T08.reasoning: Very frequent, and usually sits in the fixed pair T30 T08 at the ends of entries, which looks like a title or administrative designation.

T09.reasoning: Hatched container-like sign that often comes at the end of tablets after a fixed sign (X1972 T09, X1983 T09), as an official in a subscript would.

T10.reasoning: Elongated body with fringe strokes like fins; it appears on the same tablets as the fish-like T32 and T35.

T11.reasoning: Simple B-like sign used in many entries with other signs; no clear commodity cue.

T12.reasoning: A gabled house containing a star, the usual divine determinative, suggests a temple or household of a deity.

T13.reasoning: Shows up in herd lists (T13 T37 after T36 and T16) and in the T17/T04 fish-type lists.

T14.reasoning: Comes after many different sign groups in long name lists (X... T14), like a shared role or title.

T15.reasoning: A rectangle with lines and fringe chevrons matches the fringed-cloth sign TUG2.

T16.reasoning: The sheep sign (cross in a circle) plus an appended diamond; it sits in the fixed herd sequence after T36.

T17.reasoning: Rounded striped body with a tail fin; it heads lists alongside T38, T13, T04 that look like fish deliveries.

T18.reasoning: Like T14, it ends many differing entries in personnel-like lists.

T19.reasoning: A round or square body with a projecting stub suggests a container; contexts are mixed.

T20.reasoning: A compartmented box with a pointer; it recurs in the fixed pair X1310 T20 as a heading, possibly an institution.

T21.reasoning: Chevron sign counted in long lists of individual entries (#1 X... T21), like categories of people.

T22.reasoning: Comb-on-baseline sign often in the fixed group X1592 T22 X1587, a likely name or title complex.

T23.reasoning: Winged shape on a stick may depict a bird; contexts (T23 X0055) are ambiguous.

T24.reasoning: Diamond with spikes; it appears inside entries and at ends of tablets with no clear commodity cue.

T25.reasoning: Elongated object with a curved tail looks like an implement; contexts are mixed.

T26.reasoning: Comes at the end of entries like X0007 X1178 X0561 X0250 T26, a suffix-like use.

T27.reasoning: Very frequent inside multi-sign groups (T27 X1592, X0158 X0547 T27), behaving like part of a name.

T28.reasoning: Roof-like strokes on a long base look like a constructed object; contexts are ambiguous.

T29.reasoning: A crossed box with fringes on both sides; it is counted in large numbers like a bulk commodity.

T30.reasoning: Box with two prongs, almost always in T30 T08; it could be an institution or title.

T31.reasoning: An oval with ribs looks like a container; it is counted with numbers.

T32.reasoning: Plain fish pictogram with head, body and tail fin; it occurs with other fish-like signs T10 and T35.

T33.reasoning: Box with a comb extension; it occurs in pairs (T33 T39, T33 T15) without a clear commodity reading.

T34.reasoning: A pointed-base jar is the typical beer-jug shape; it is frequent and counted.

T35.reasoning: Like T17 (a striped D-shape) but with no tail, and it sits on tablets with the fish signs T10 and T32.

T36.reasoning: A cross in a rounded square is the sheep sign, and it heads the herd lists (T36, X0147, X1844, T16, X1166, T06).

T37.reasoning: Appears in herd tablets after T36 and T16, often as T13 T37 with counts.

T38.reasoning: Forked lines, possibly a tail; it occurs in the T17/T13 fish-like lists.

T39.reasoning: A gridded rectangle with lines like the fringed cloth T15, suggesting a woven textile or a field.

T40.reasoning: Comb-like shaft with an arc, related in form to T07; it appears in compounds (T20 T40, T40 X0622).
